issues.description: The problem statement and UML explicitly require the Farm to hold animals in a List and to initialize it using an ArrayList in the no-arg constructor, but the reference solution implements the animals collection as a Queue backed by a LinkedList (and its getter/setter use Queue). This contradicts the exercise instructions and UML and could confuse students about which collection type they must use and how to initialize it.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution (and template examples) with the problem statement: change the Farm implementation in the solution to use a List<Animal> and initialize it with new ArrayList<>() in the no-arg constructor, and update the getter/setter to use List<Animal>. Alternatively, if Queue/LinkedList is preferred, update the problem statement and UML to state Queue/LinkedList instead of List/ArrayList so all artifacts match.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify the Farm's collection of animals as a List<Animal> and explicitly instruct using an ArrayList initialized in the no-argument constructor, but the reference solution declares the animals attribute as a Queue<Animal> and initializes it with a LinkedList. The template Farm.java also lacks a concrete animals attribute and contains TODOs referring to printing animal types. This mismatch in the collection type/implementation (List/ArrayList vs Queue/LinkedList) creates a mapping confusion: students are told to implement an ArrayList-based List but the solution uses a different collection type and methods (offer() vs add()), which may mislead or frustrate learners trying to follow the specification and compare with the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the repository implementations with the problem statement: change the solution (and update the template) to declare the animals attribute as List<Animal> and initialize it with new ArrayList<>() in the no-argument constructor, and use List-compatible operations (add(), iteration). Alternatively, if Queue semantics were intended, update the problem statement and UML to specify Queue<Animal> and LinkedList so all artifacts use the same collection type.
